name: Magog
overview: Magog is a male figure identified in Scripture as a son of Japheth. Beyond this unique attribute, there are no additional tribal affiliations or personal notes recorded about him. His mention is concise and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Magog appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:2. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to this name in the biblical text, so it is presented plainly as a personal name without further elaboration.
familyAndRelationships: Magog is recorded as a son of Japheth, making him part of Noah's lineage through Japheth. Scripture does not provide additional family relationships or descendants for Magog beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Magog's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of Genesis 10, which traces the descendants of Noah and the repopulation of the earth after the Flood. As a son of Japheth, Magog contributes to the biblical understanding of the nations and peoples that emerged from Noah's family. His mention underscores God's providential plan in preserving humanity through Noah's lineage.
